title: Oktoberfest funding request and 2025 mid-year update
subtitle: Accommodation tax reserve questions, updated records retention by-law, and capital budget amendments for 2025.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee heard from KW Oktoberfest, whose organizers said a lower Cultural Drivers of Tourism grant and rising security costs are straining the festival. The committee directed staff to report back to Council in September with options for restoring annual funding to the historical $65,000, including using the Regional share of the Municipal Accommodation Tax (MAT) in 2025 {{vote:m1}}. Staff said the MAT reserve holds about $400,000, with large event requests expected soon.

The committee also received the 2025 mid-year update on the Region's Annual Business Plan and recommended capital budget amendments {{vote:m4}}. Staff reported no major risks to the plan's objectives, though growth, policy changes and economic uncertainty continue to put pressure on finances and services.

Other recommendations include an updated Records Retention By-law and the consent agenda {{vote:m2}}. Because this is a committee, these items go to Regional Council for a final decision. The Oktoberfest report is due at Council in September, before the festival begins.

decisions.detail: The committee directed staff to report to Council in September on restoring annual funding to the historical $65,000 for Oktoberfest, including using the Regional portion of the MAT in 2025.
The committee recommended that Council receive the 2025 Mid-Year Update on the Annual Business Plan and amend the 2025 Capital Budget and 2026-2034 Capital Forecast for projects listed in Appendix D.
The committee recommended that Council approve the updated by-law setting retention periods for Regional records and repealing By-law 93-076.
The committee received the consent agenda items for information and approved them, with no items removed for separate discussion.

debate: Oktoberfest representatives said the grant formula and its 3% budget cap do not reflect the festival's year-round work or its support for other festivals. They said a lower grant, plus rising police and vehicle-barrier costs, could force choices about free events such as the parade.
Some councillors questioned whether police costs should fall entirely on the festival. Others stressed the festival's community benefits, including fundraising and shared equipment with other events.

Several councillors worried that changing course after the grant criteria were set would invite requests from other groups that received less than they wanted. Supporters said the festival is foundational to the region and asked staff to examine policy and sustainability, not only a one-time fix.

Staff said MAT revenue fluctuates with hotel stays and that the reserve may be drawn down by large one-time event requests. One councillor suggested reducing any Ontario Summer Games request to keep Oktoberfest whole. Staff and the chair preferred to leave the motion unchanged and address this in the report.

On the mid-year report, one councillor questioned the proposed amendment to the capital forecast because the forecast changes were not shown. Staff said forecast impacts would be reviewed through the budget process. Another councillor asked whether the figures include ION Stage 2 or the hospital donation, and staff said they do not.
